excerpt: BPI Baguio Arabica Caturra coffee is an arabica coffee variety, also sold or known as Caturra or Arabica Caturra. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2008 as NSIC 2008 Cf A 06. BPI Baguio NCRDC bred it.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Caturra or Arabica Caturra, this is the same coffee. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [coffee variety finder](/crop-varieties/coffee), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. It first bore fruit about 36 months after planting. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** First flowers and fruit about 36 months after planting.
**Yield:** About 1.85 kg fresh (0.61 kg dry) per tree.
**Fruit:** Red oblong berries, Class A, strong flavor and aroma.
**Where:** Selected at the BPI Baguio station.
Short tree, about 1.1 m at 7 years.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the higher yielding of BPI Baguio's registered Arabicas, but rust susceptible. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant BPI Baguio Arabica Caturra coffee

Arabica wants cool highland air, robusta grows in the lowlands, and liberica, the barako, and excelsa are hardy in between. Pick the species for your elevation first, then a selection by yield and cup quality. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Caturra the same as BPI Baguio Arabica Caturra?
items.a: Yes. Caturra is another name for BPI Baguio Arabica Caturra, registered as NSIC 2008 Cf A 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of BPI Baguio Arabica Caturra?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
